accepted.question_text: Let W be a symplectic manifold of bounded Hofer-Zehnder capacity, and let H: W -> R be a smooth proper Hamiltonian. If AP_H denotes the set of regular values a for which the energy level {H = a} carries no periodic orbit, how large can the set AP_H be?
accepted.context_brief: Size of the aperiodic value set

evidence.quote: We call a value a of H aperiodic if the level {H = a} carries no periodic orbits. Let W be a symplectic manifold of bounded capacity and H a smooth proper function on W. How large can the set AP_H of regular aperiodic values of H be?

accepted.question_text: For the standard symplectic torus T^{2n} with n > 1, is the Hofer-Zehnder capacity finite?
accepted.context_brief: Capacity of the standard symplectic torus

evidence.quote: It seems to be unknown whether or not T2n with the standard symplectic structure has finite capacity for n > 1.

accepted.question_text: For 2n >= 6, let K be a compact zero-measure subset of (0, infinity). Does there exist a C-infinity Hamiltonian H: R^{2n} -> R that is C^0-close and compactly supported isotopic to the quadratic irrational-ellipsoid Hamiltonian H_0 = sum lambda_j |z_j|^2 with positive rationally independent coefficients lambda_j, such that the Hamiltonian flow of H has no closed trajectories for every energy value in K?
accepted.context_brief: Aperiodic energy values on a zero-measure set

evidence.quote: The next step is more subtle. It appears plausible that the function H0 can be modified as in the proof of Theorem 3.1 simultaneously for all energy values from a compact zero measure set K subset (0, infinity). The resulting function H will then be smoothly isotopic to H0 and have K as the set of aperiodic values.

Conjecture 3.4. For 2n >= 6, there exists a C infinity-function H : R2n -> R, C 0-close and isotopic (with a compact support) to H0, such that the Hamiltonian flow of H has no closed trajectories for energy values in the set K.

An irrational ellipsoid M in the standard symplectic vector space Cn is the unit energy level of the quadratic Hamiltonian H0 = sum lambda_j |z_j|^2, where the eigenvalues lambda_j are positive and rationally independent.

accepted.question_text: Can G. Kuperberg's C^1-smooth divergence-free vector field on S^3 be realized by a C^2 embedding, or even by a C^1 embedding, of S^3 into R^4? A positive answer would produce a C^2-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in dimension four.

evidence.quote: A C 1-smooth divergence-free vector field on S 3 was found by G. Kuperberg, [KuG]. It is not known whether or not this vector field can be obtained by a C 2- (or even C 1-) embedding of S 3 into R4. Such an embedding would give a C 2-smooth 'counterexample' to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in dimension four.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a compact Riemannian manifold equipped with a symplectic two-form sigma, let omega = omega_0 + pi^* sigma be the induced twisted symplectic form on T^*M, and let H be the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian. Must a neighborhood of the zero section M in T^*M have finite Hofer-Zehnder capacity? Moreover, do almost all levels of H carry periodic orbits, and, when sigma is symplectic, does every sufficiently low energy level of H carry a contractible periodic orbit?
accepted.context_brief: Twisted geodesic flows near the zero section

evidence.quote: Consider a compact Riemannian manifold M equipped with a closed two-form sigma. Denote by omega_0 the standard symplectic form on T^* M and by pi : T^* M -> M the natural projection. The form omega = omega_0 + pi^* sigma on T^* M is symplectic (a twisted symplectic structure). The flow of the standard metric Hamiltonian H (the kinetic energy) on (T^* M, omega) describes the motion of a charge on M in the magnetic field sigma.

Conjecture 4.2. For every M and any symplectic form sigma, a neighborhood of M in T^* M has finite Hofer-Zehnder capacity. Moreover, almost all levels of H carry periodic orbits. When sigma is symplectic, every low energy level of H has a contractible periodic orbit.

accepted.question_text: In the horocycle-flow example where M is a compact surface of genus g >= 2 with constant curvature -1 and sigma is the area form, so that the twisted geodesic flow on the level {H = 1} has no periodic orbits, do the sublevel sets {H < a} with a > 1 have finite Hofer-Zehnder capacity?

evidence.quote: Let M be a compact surface of genus g >= 2 equipped with a metric of constant negative curvature K = -1. Let sigma be the area form on M. Then the Hamiltonian flow on the energy level {H = 1} has no periodic orbits.
For example, it is not known whether in the setting of Example 4.1 the sets {H < a} with a > 1 have finite capacity.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a twisted geodesic flow with more than one aperiodic energy level?
accepted.context_brief: Multiple aperiodic levels for twisted geodesic flows

evidence.quote: Example 4.1 is the only known 'naturally arising' example of a Hamiltonian flow with a regular compact aperiodic energy level. Furthermore, this is the only known example of a twisted geodesic flow with an aperiodic energy level. It is not known if there exists a twisted geodesic flow with more than one aperiodic energy level.
